Try Pro free before you decide

Try every Pro feature free for [tw_value key="trial_days"] days. [tw_value key="trial_card_policy"] The trial runs on one site and includes paid AI models, advanced search, and analytics and inbox.

When the trial ends, you choose. Upgrade with the same license key and keep every setting, or stay on the free plan. Your scan, your chats, and your leads stay where they are either way.

We send reminder emails before the trial ends, so nothing changes by surprise. If you have questions during the trial, our docs and support are there to help you get the most out of it.

Compare every Talkwyn plan

Every plan, free included, scans your site, answers in your visitor's language, and captures leads inside the chat. Pro adds paid AI models, advanced search, and analytics and inbox. The Agency plan adds white label, copied settings, and a lead inbox per client.

[tw_compare_plans]

Founding customer pricing

Talkwyn is a new company, and we are building it with our first customers. The first [tw_value key="founding_seats"] customers keep their price locked in for as long as they renew. They also get direct access to the people building the product, and a real say in what we build next.

[tw_founding style="band"]

Why Talkwyn pricing stays low over time

Most hosted chat tools charge every month, and many charge more as your conversations grow. Talkwyn runs inside your own site and uses the AI provider you choose. That makes the yearly license your only fixed cost.

AI usage is paid to your provider, not to us. Groq, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, and Cloudflare Workers AI all offer free tiers, and Talkwyn can switch between them when one hits its limit. Limits are set by each provider and change, so check their pages for current numbers.

[tw_cost_explainer]

Thinking about another tool?

We wrote fair, side by side pages so you can check the structural differences yourself: where your data lives, how you pay, and who picks the AI. Start with our AI chatbot comparison guide, or go straight to the Tidio alternative page.

Recommend Talkwyn to clients or followers? Join Talkwyn Partners and earn a commission on every paid plan you refer. Building sites for clients? See the white label chatbot for agencies.

Talkwyn pricing questions

Can I move my license to another site?

Yes. Deactivate the old site from Talkwyn's settings or from your account, and the slot is free again for a new site.

How does the free trial work?

Try every Pro feature free for [tw_value key="trial_days"] days. [tw_value key="trial_card_policy"] It covers one site. At the end, upgrade with the same key or keep using the free plan. Nothing is lost.

Can I get a refund?

Yes. If Pro is not right for you, ask within [tw_value key="refund_days"] days of purchase and we refund it. The license is then deactivated and Talkwyn keeps working with the free features. Read the refund policy.

How do renewals work?

Pro licenses are yearly. We email you 30 days and 7 days before your license expires, with a one-click renewal link. If you do not renew, Talkwyn keeps working with the free features, and Pro features pause until you renew.

Can I upgrade later?

Yes, any time. Open your license in your account and pick a bigger plan. You pay only the difference for the time left, and you keep the same license key.

Do staging and local sites count toward my limit?

No. Staging and local sites never count toward your site limit, so you can test changes before they go live without using a slot.

What do the AI answers cost?

Talkwyn does not charge per conversation. You connect your own AI provider, and several offer free tiers that suit many small business sites. Greetings and small talk do not use your AI quota at all. See the free AI keys guide.

and the large backpack, is it in stock?

Tidio is a hosted customer service tool that combines live chat, a shared inbox, and AI answers. You create an account on their service, add their widget to your site, and they run the hosting and the AI for you. It works on many website platforms, not only WordPress.

Talkwyn is an AI chatbot that runs inside your own site. It is live today as a WordPress plugin that works with WooCommerce and reads Elementor content. You install it, click Scan my site, paste an AI key, and it is live in about five minutes. It answers business questions only from your own content, with source links under each answer.

They want their data at home

Talkwyn stores chats and leads in your own WordPress database. Messages go only to the AI provider you picked.

Their customers mix languages

Talkwyn replies in the language of each message, handles Roman Urdu and mixed messages, and shows Arabic and Urdu right to left.

They prefer a yearly license

One license per year, and a free plan that never expires. No bill that grows with every conversation.

They want answers from the site itself

Talkwyn scans your pages and products and keeps the index fresh when you edit, so you do not maintain a separate knowledge base.

If the answer is not on your site, Talkwyn says so and offers to connect the visitor with your team. It never invents a price or a policy.

  • You prefer the vendor to manage hosting and AI for you, with no AI key to set up.

It depends on what you need. If you want an AI chatbot that runs inside WordPress, answers from your own content, and keeps data on your site, Talkwyn is built for that. If you need human live chat first, Tidio may suit you better.

Yes. The free plan includes the site scan, multilingual answers, lead capture, chat history, and free AI providers. Try every Pro feature free for [tw_value key="trial_days"] days. [tw_value key="trial_card_policy"]

Talkwyn focuses on AI answers and lead capture. When a visitor needs a person, it offers a short form inside the chat, and the lead is saved in WordPress and emailed to you right away.

You can install Talkwyn alongside your current tool and compare answers. Show only one chat widget to visitors at a time, so they are not confused.

Talkwyn and Intercom in one paragraph each

Intercom is a customer service platform for support teams. It brings together a help desk, a shared inbox, messaging, and AI features, with workflows for teams that handle a lot of conversations. It is hosted, and it is designed for companies with dedicated support staff.

Talkwyn is an AI chatbot that runs inside your own site. It is live today as a WordPress plugin that works with WooCommerce and reads Elementor content. It answers business questions from your own pages, in the visitor's language, and when a person is needed, it captures the lead and emails it to you. Setup takes about five minutes.

If you have a support team of many people, you are probably comparing help desks. If you are a clinic, a store, an agency, or a two-person business, you may simply need a chatbot that answers well and hands you leads.

If you run Talkwyn on your site, mention it and your chosen AI provider in your own privacy policy.

We protect talkwyn.com with encrypted connections, access controls, and regular updates. IP addresses sent to the license server are stored hashed, not in plain form. No system is perfectly secure, so if you believe your account has been misused, contact the Talkwyn team right away. [Describe breach notification process.]

A scripted chatbot needs you to write every question and answer by hand, then breaks the first time someone phrases things differently. Many hosted chat tools send your content and your customers' messages to their servers and charge you every month.

It gets harder when your visitors speak more than one language. Someone writes in Arabic, someone types in Roman Urdu, someone asks in Spanish. Most chat widgets reply in English, or not at all.

title: Free AI API Keys in 2026: How to Get a Groq API Key and Other Free Options for Your Chatbot
excerpt: Where to get a Groq API key and other free AI API keys, what free tiers really mean, and how to use two keys so your chatbot never goes quiet.
content:
A Groq API key is one of the easiest ways to give your website chatbot a brain without paying for AI. This guide shows you how to get a Groq API key, plus free keys from Google Gemini, OpenRouter, and Cloudflare, and how to plug them into the WordPress chatbot plugin Talkwyn so your chatbot keeps answering even when one provider is busy.

[tw_icon name="badge-check" size="16"] Facts and prices checked October 2026. Verify on each vendor's page before you decide.

On this page

  1. What an AI API key is (in plain words)
  2. How to get a Groq API key, step by step
  3. Other free AI API key options
  4. What "free tier" really means, and why limits change
  5. Is there an unlimited free AI API key?
  6. How to keep your API keys safe
  7. Use two keys for automatic fallback in Talkwyn
  8. When to move to a paid model

What an AI API key is (in plain words)

An API key is a long string of letters and numbers that works like a password for software. When your chatbot needs to write an answer, it sends the visitor's question to an AI provider. The key tells the provider who is asking, which account the request belongs to, and how much that account is allowed to use.

You do not need to be a developer to use one. You create the key on the provider's website, copy it, and paste it into your chatbot's settings. That's it. The chatbot does the rest.

Two things are worth knowing from day one:

  • A key is tied to your account. Anyone who has it can use your quota, so treat it like a password.
  • Each provider sets its own rules. How many requests you can send, which models you can use, and what is free are all decided by the provider, not by your chatbot.

How to get a Groq API key, step by step

Groq runs open AI models and is known for fast replies, which suits a chat window where visitors expect an answer in seconds. Getting a Groq API key takes a couple of minutes.

  1. Go to console.groq.com/keys and sign in or create an account.
  2. On the API keys page, choose to create a new key.
  3. Give it a name you will recognize later, like "My website chatbot".
  4. Copy the key right away. It is shown only once. If you lose it, delete it and create a new one.
  5. Paste the key into your chatbot's AI provider settings and save.
Tip: name each key after the site that uses it. If you ever need to turn one off, you will know which site it belongs to.

Other free AI API key options

A Groq API key is a great start, but it should not be your only one. Here are three more providers that offer free tiers, with the steps we are sure of. Screens change from time to time, so if a button has moved, look for a page called "API keys" or "Keys".

Google Gemini (Google AI Studio)

  1. Go to aistudio.google.com/app/apikey and sign in with a Google account.
  2. Choose to create an API key.
  3. Copy the key and store it somewhere safe, like a password manager.
  4. Paste it into your chatbot as a Gemini provider.

Gemini is a good second choice because it comes from a different company than Groq. If one provider has a busy hour, the other usually does not.

OpenRouter

  1. Go to openrouter.ai/settings/keys and sign in or create an account.
  2. Create a new key and give it a name.
  3. Copy the key once and keep it safe.
  4. Paste it into your chatbot as an OpenRouter provider.

OpenRouter gives you one key that reaches models from many companies. Some models are marked as free on OpenRouter. Check which ones are free today before you choose one, because that list changes.

Cloudflare Workers AI

  1. Sign in to the Cloudflare dashboard.
  2. Find and copy your Account ID.
  3. Create an API token that is allowed to use Workers AI.
  4. Copy the token once and keep it safe.
  5. Paste both the Account ID and the token into your chatbot as a Cloudflare provider.

Cloudflare needs two values instead of one. That is the only extra step, and it is worth it if you already use Cloudflare for your site.

What "free tier" really means, and why limits change

A free tier is an allowance, not a promise. Each provider lets free accounts send a certain number of requests, or use a certain amount of text, in a given time. Go over it and the provider pauses your requests until the window resets, or asks you to add billing.

We do not list the numbers here, on purpose. Providers change their free limits often, sometimes with little notice, and different models on the same account can have different limits. A number we printed today could be wrong next month. Instead:

  • Open each provider's own limits or pricing page before you choose.
  • Check the limits for the exact model you plan to use, not just the account.
  • Look again every few months, or when your chatbot starts getting more traffic.
  • Assume any free tier can shrink, and plan a backup.

For many small business sites, a free tier is enough for everyday questions. A busy week, a sale, or a mention on social media can push you over. That is why the next two sections matter.

Is there an unlimited free AI API key?

No. Searches for a "free AI API key unlimited" are common, and the honest answer is that no reputable provider offers unlimited AI for free. Running AI models costs real money in hardware and electricity, so every free tier has a ceiling.

Be careful with websites or posts that offer "unlimited" keys. They are often shared keys taken from someone else's account, which can stop working at any moment, break the provider's terms, and expose your visitors' messages to a stranger. Use only keys you create yourself, on the provider's own website.

The practical way to get close to "never runs out" is to combine several free keys from different providers. Each one has its own allowance, and your chatbot moves to the next one when the first is full.

How to keep your API keys safe

A leaked key can drain your quota or, if you have billing turned on, run up a bill. A few habits keep you safe:

  • Paste keys only into your chatbot's settings. Never put a key in a page, a post, a theme file, or a public code repository.
  • One key per site. If one site has a problem, you can turn off that key without touching the others.
  • Store keys in a password manager, not in email, chat messages, or a shared document.
  • Do not send keys to anyone, including people who say they are support staff. You can always create a fresh key for a trusted developer and delete it later.
  • Delete keys you no longer use. Old keys are easy to forget and easy to misuse.
  • If you think a key leaked, delete it and create a new one. Then paste the new key into your chatbot.

In Talkwyn, keys are stored in your own WordPress site, and messages go only to the AI provider you picked. Talkwyn does not route your visitors' messages through anyone else.

Use two keys for automatic fallback in Talkwyn

Here is where free keys become reliable. Talkwyn lets you add more than one AI provider. Put your favorite first. When that provider hits its limit or is busy, Talkwyn switches to the next one automatically and remembers which one is working, so visitors do not see an error.

If every provider is busy at the same moment, Talkwyn still replies with the most relevant information it found on your site, so nobody is left staring at a spinner.

  1. Create a Groq API key and a second key from another provider, such as Google Gemini.
  2. In your WordPress dashboard, open Talkwyn's AI provider settings.
  3. Add Groq and paste its key.
  4. Add the second provider and paste its key.
  5. Put the provider you prefer at the top of the list and save.
  6. Ask your chatbot a question on your site to confirm it answers.

Talkwyn also handles greetings and small talk without calling the AI at all, so "hi" and "thanks" do not use up your free quota. The guide to choosing an AI provider explains the order Talkwyn tries providers in, and what changes with paid models.

If you have not set up a chatbot yet, follow our step-by-step guide on how to add a free AI chatbot to WordPress. It takes about five minutes.

When to move to a paid model

Free keys are a great way to start. You might want a paid model if your site gets a lot of questions every day, if you need the best possible quality in a less common language, or if you want predictable capacity during busy seasons. Language quality depends on the model you choose, so test your main languages either way.

Talkwyn Pro adds OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Mistral, and DeepSeek. You can try every Pro feature with a free Talkwyn Pro trial for [tw_value key="trial_days"] days. [tw_value key="trial_card_policy"] When the trial ends, you can upgrade or keep using the free plan with your free keys.

Groq API key FAQ

Is a Groq API key free?

Creating a Groq API key is free, and Groq offers a free tier for its models. The free tier has limits that Groq sets and can change, so check Groq's current limits page before you rely on it.

How do I get a Groq API key?

Sign in at console.groq.com/keys, create a new key, give it a name, and copy it right away. It is shown only once.

Is there an unlimited free AI API key?

No. Every honest free tier has limits, because running AI models costs money. The closest you can get is adding keys from several providers so your chatbot switches when one is full.

Which free AI API key should I use for a chatbot?

Start with a Groq API key, then add a second key from Google Gemini, OpenRouter, or Cloudflare as a backup. Using two different companies makes it less likely both are busy at the same time.

Can someone steal my API key from my website?

Not if you keep it in your chatbot's settings. Talkwyn stores keys in your WordPress site and never prints them in your pages. Never paste a key into page content or a public file.

What happens when my free limit runs out?

The provider pauses requests until the limit resets. In Talkwyn, a second provider takes over automatically, and if every provider is busy it still replies with relevant information from your site.

title: How to Add a Free AI Chatbot for Your WordPress Website (Step by Step)
excerpt: A step-by-step guide to adding a free AI chatbot to your WordPress website, from install to your first lead.
content:
You can add a chatbot for website visitors free of monthly fees, and it takes about five minutes on WordPress. This guide walks you through every step with Talkwyn, a free WordPress chatbot plugin: install it, scan your site, add a free AI key, make it look like your brand, test it with real questions, and start collecting leads.

On this page

  1. Why add a chatbot to your website?
  2. What you need before you start
  3. How to create a chatbot for your website that actually helps
  4. Step 1: Install the free WordPress chatbot plugin
  5. Step 2: Scan your site
  6. Step 3: Add a free AI key
  7. Step 4: Make it look like your brand
  8. Step 5: Test your free chatbot for website visitors with 10 real questions
  9. Step 6: Turn on lead capture
  10. Common mistakes to avoid
  11. After launch: the first two weeks
  12. Free plan or Pro?

Why add a chatbot to your website?

Most visitors leave with a question nobody answered. They want to know your opening hours, whether you deliver to their area, or how much a service costs. If the answer is not easy to find, they go back to the search results and pick someone else.

A good AI chatbot answers those questions on the spot, using the content you already published. It works at night and on weekends, and it can reply in the visitor's own language. When someone is ready to buy or book, it offers to pass their details to your team.

  • Answers from your own pages, with links to the source.
  • Replies in the language each visitor writes in.
  • Turns serious questions into leads you can follow up.
  • Admits when it does not know, instead of guessing.

What you need before you start

  • A WordPress website where you can log in as an administrator.
  • Published content that answers common questions: services, prices, hours, shipping, contact details. The chatbot can only answer from what is on your site.
  • A free AI key from Groq, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, or Cloudflare. You will create one in step 3.
  • About five minutes.

You do not need to write code, train a model, or upload documents by hand.

How to create a chatbot for your website that actually helps

The quality of your chatbot depends on the quality of your pages. Spend ten minutes on these before you install anything, and your first answers will be much better.

  • Write down the questions you hear most. Look at your inbox, your phone notes, and your contact form. Most businesses get the same ten to twenty questions again and again.
  • Make sure each one has an answer on a published page. A short FAQ page is often the quickest fix.
  • Put prices, hours, and policies in plain text. Clear sentences are easier to find and quote than details hidden in an image.
  • Keep one source of truth. If your delivery fee appears on three pages with three different numbers, fix that first.
  • Add your contact details and service area so the chatbot can point people to the right place.

Step 1: Install the free WordPress chatbot plugin

  1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins, then Add New.
  2. Search for Talkwyn.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.

A new Talkwyn item appears in your dashboard menu. Open it to continue.

Step 2: Scan your site

Click Scan my site. Talkwyn reads your published pages, posts, menus, custom fields, and Elementor content. If you run WooCommerce, it also reads your products, including price, stock status, and attributes.

It never reads drafts, users, or passwords. After the first scan, Talkwyn keeps its index up to date when you edit or publish content, so you do not have to scan again every time you change a price.

Step 3: Add a free AI key

Talkwyn sends each question to an AI provider you choose. Several providers have free tiers. Our guide to free AI API keys, including how to get a Groq API key, shows each step.

  1. Create a key with Groq, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, or Cloudflare.
  2. In Talkwyn's AI provider settings, add the provider and paste the key.
  3. Add a second provider if you can. Talkwyn switches automatically when one hits its limit.
Free limits are set by each provider and change over time. Check each provider's own limits page, and add two keys so your chatbot keeps answering on busy days.

Step 4: Make it look like your brand

Pick a color that matches your site, choose an avatar, and write a short welcome message. Keep the welcome message specific. "Hi! Ask me about our prices, opening hours, or delivery areas" works better than "How can I help?" because it shows visitors what the chatbot knows.

You can also hide the chatbot on pages where it would get in the way, like checkout or thank-you pages. When everything looks right, turn it on.

Step 5: Test your free chatbot for website visitors with 10 real questions

Open your site in a private browser window and ask the questions real customers ask. Here are 10 to start with. Swap in your own details.

  1. What are your opening hours?
  2. How much does [your main service or product] cost?
  3. Do you deliver to [a nearby town]?
  4. What is your return or cancellation policy?
  5. Is [a product] in stock in a large size?
  6. And how much is that one? (a follow-up, to check it remembers the last question)
  7. Where are you located, and is there parking?
  8. Can I book an appointment for tomorrow?
  9. Do you offer something you do not offer? (it should say it does not know and offer to connect you with your team)
  10. The same opening hours question in another language your customers use, such as Spanish or Arabic.

For each answer, check three things: is it correct, is there a source link under it, and does it point to the right page? If an answer is wrong or missing, the fix is almost always on your site. Add or update the page that should answer it, and Talkwyn picks up the change.

Talkwyn detects the language of each message and replies in the same language, including Roman Urdu and mixed messages. See how it works on the multilingual chatbot page.

Step 6: Turn on lead capture

Lead capture is part of the free plan. When a visitor shows buying intent, like "can I book?", "what's the price?", or "call me", Talkwyn asks if they would like a follow-up from your team. If they say yes, a short form opens inside the chat.

  • Make sure lead capture is turned on in Talkwyn's settings.
  • Check the email address where new leads are sent.
  • Send a test lead yourself and confirm the email arrives.

Every lead is saved in your WordPress site and emailed to you instantly, and you can export leads as CSV. Learn more about lead generation with Talkwyn.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Thin content. If your prices or policies are not on your site, the chatbot cannot answer them. It will not invent them.
  • Only one AI key. A single free tier can run out on a busy day. Add a second provider.
  • A vague welcome message. Tell visitors what they can ask.
  • Skipping the test. Ten questions take ten minutes and catch most gaps.
  • Forgetting other languages. If your customers write in Arabic, Urdu, or Spanish, test in those languages. Quality depends on the AI model you chose.
  • Showing it everywhere. Hide it on checkout and thank-you pages so it does not distract buyers.
  • Not checking the lead email. A lead that lands in spam is a lead lost.

After launch: the first two weeks

A chatbot gets better as your content gets better. Set aside a few minutes each week for the first couple of weeks.

  1. Read through your chat history and note any question the chatbot could not answer.
  2. Add or update the page that should answer it. Talkwyn keeps its index up to date when you edit.
  3. Look at your leads. Did each one get a reply from your team the same day?
  4. Check that your AI providers are still working, and add a second one if you have not yet.
  5. Ask a few questions yourself again, in each language your customers use.

After that, a quick monthly check is usually enough. Visitors will tell you, through their questions, what your website is missing.

Free plan or Pro?

The free plan includes the site scan, multilingual answers, lead capture, chat history, and free AI providers. Pro adds paid AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Mistral, and DeepSeek), advanced search, analytics, and an inbox. You can try every Pro feature for [tw_value key="trial_days"] days. Yes. Talkwyn's free plan is free forever and works with free AI keys from providers like Groq and Google Gemini. Those providers set their own free limits.

Install a WordPress chatbot plugin like Talkwyn, click Scan my site, paste an AI key, and turn it on. No code is needed.

title: Real Estate Chatbot Template: 25 Questions, Answers, and a Lead Flow (Free Download)
excerpt: 25 real buyer and renter questions with example answers, a lead flow, after-hours scripts, an Arabic example, and a printable checklist.
content:
This real estate chatbot template gives you the 25 questions buyers and renters ask most, an example answer for each, a simple lead qualification flow, after-hours scripts, and a printable checklist. Use it to plan the content your website needs before you switch on a real estate chatbot.

On this page

  1. How to use this real estate chatbot template
  2. 25 questions with example answers
  3. The lead qualification flow
  4. After-hours scripts
  5. A multilingual example: English and Arabic
  6. Download the checklist
  7. What makes the best real estate chatbot?

How to use this real estate chatbot template

An AI chatbot like Talkwyn answers from your own website. So the template is really a content plan: for each question, make sure a page on your site holds the answer. Then the chatbot can reply with the right details and a link to that page.

Every answer below is an example to adapt. Replace the details in brackets with your own. None of it is legal or financial advice. For mortgage and legal questions, the best answer points the visitor to a qualified adviser.

25 questions with example answers

Listings (questions 1 to 6)

  1. Do you have 2-bedroom apartments for rent in [area]? Example answer: "Yes, here are the 2-bedroom rentals in [area] listed right now, with links to each one. Would you like me to arrange a viewing?"
  2. What is the price of the house on [street]? Example answer: "The asking price is shown on the listing page here. Prices can change, so the agent will confirm the latest figure when you speak."
  3. Is this property still available? Example answer: "It is listed as available on our site. Availability changes quickly, so I can ask an agent to confirm today."
  4. Do you have anything under [budget]? Example answer: "Here are the current listings within that budget. Tell me the area you prefer and I can narrow it down."
  5. Are pets allowed? Example answer: "Pet rules depend on the landlord or building. This listing says [pet policy]. An agent can check for any you are interested in."
  6. Is it furnished? Example answer: "This one is listed as [furnished, part-furnished, or unfurnished]. The full list of what is included is on the listing page."

Viewings (questions 7 to 10)

  1. Can I book a viewing this weekend? Example answer: "Our agents run viewings on [days and times]. Leave your name and number and we will confirm a slot."
  2. Do you offer video viewings? Example answer: "Yes, we offer [video tours or live video calls] for most listings. I can pass your request to an agent."
  3. How long does a viewing take? Example answer: "Most viewings take about [time]. Allow a little longer if you want to see the area too."
  4. Can I bring my family or a builder? Example answer: "Of course. Just let us know how many people are coming when you book."

Mortgage basics (questions 11 to 15)

Keep these answers general and always point to a qualified mortgage adviser. Your chatbot should never tell someone what they can borrow.

  1. How much deposit do I need? Example answer: "It depends on the lender and your situation. A qualified mortgage adviser can tell you what applies to you. Would you like us to introduce one?"
  2. Can you help me get a mortgage? Example answer: "We work with [partner adviser or broker]. They can talk you through your options. I can pass on your details."
  3. What is a mortgage in principle? Example answer: "It is an early indication from a lender of how much they might lend. A mortgage adviser can explain the process and whether you need one."
  4. Can I buy if I am self-employed or new to the country? Example answer: "Often yes, but lenders have different rules. A qualified adviser is the best person to check."
  5. What are the extra costs of buying? Example answer: "There are usually fees on top of the price, such as [list the common ones in your market]. Our buying guide explains them, and an adviser can give exact figures."

Areas (questions 16 to 20)

  1. Which areas do you cover? Example answer: "We cover [areas]. Here is our areas page with listings in each one."
  2. Is [area] good for families? Example answer: "Our [area] guide covers schools, parks, and transport nearby. An agent who knows the area can answer more specific questions."
  3. How far is it from [landmark or business district]? Example answer: "The listing page shows the location on a map. Our area guide lists the main transport links."
  4. Are there schools nearby? Example answer: "Our [area] guide lists schools near this property. Check each school's own website for admissions."
  5. Is parking included? Example answer: "This listing includes [parking details]. If it is not mentioned, I can ask the agent."

Paperwork (questions 21 to 25)

  1. What documents do I need to rent? Example answer: "Most landlords ask for [ID, proof of income, references]. Our renting guide has the full list for our area."
  2. How long does a purchase usually take? Example answer: "Timelines vary a lot. Our buying guide explains the main steps, and your lawyer or conveyancer can give a better estimate for your case."
  3. Do I need a lawyer? Example answer: "Most buyers use a lawyer or conveyancer. We cannot give legal advice, but we can share contacts if you would like."
  4. How much is the security deposit? Example answer: "The deposit for this listing is shown on its page. Rules on deposits depend on local law, so ask the agent if anything is unclear."
  5. Can I sign the lease online? Example answer: "We offer [online signing or in-office signing]. An agent will guide you through it once your application is accepted."
These are example answers to adapt, not advice. Talkwyn only answers business questions from your own content and never invents a price or a policy. If a page is missing, it says it does not know and offers to connect the visitor with your team.

The lead qualification flow

Good real estate leads need four things. Ask for them in this order, one at a time, and only after you have helped the visitor with their question.

  1. Budget. "To show you the right homes, what price range are you looking at?"
  2. Area. "Which areas are you most interested in?"
  3. Timeline. "When are you hoping to move?"
  4. Contact. "Would you like an agent to call or message you? If so, I just need your name and phone number or email."

Talkwyn detects buying intent in many languages, such as "can I book a viewing?" or "call me", and asks before it shows a short form inside the chat. Leads are saved in WordPress and emailed to you instantly. See lead generation with Talkwyn for the details.

After-hours scripts

Many property searches happen in the evening. Put these lines on your contact or FAQ page so the chatbot can use them. They are examples to adapt.

  • Office closed: "Our office is closed right now and opens at [time]. I can answer questions about our listings, or take your details so an agent calls you first thing."
  • Urgent viewing: "I cannot confirm a viewing time myself, but I can send your request to the team now. You will hear back when the office opens at [time]."
  • Maintenance issue (tenants): "For emergencies like a leak or no power, call [emergency number]. For anything else, leave the details here and we will reply during office hours."
  • Weekend: "We run viewings on [days]. Leave your name and number and we will suggest a time."

A multilingual example: English and Arabic

Many buyers and renters prefer to ask in their own language. Talkwyn detects the language of each message and replies in the same one, and Arabic displays right to left with readable fonts. Names, prices, and emails stay as they are. Here is an example conversation for a sample agency, with an English translation.

content:
There are a lot of WordPress chatbot plugins, and they solve different problems. This guide compares nine of them on five plain criteria. One thing first: we make Talkwyn, a WordPress chatbot plugin, so we are not neutral. We list the tools in alphabetical order, explain our criteria, and tell you when another tool is the better pick.

  8. Questions to ask any chatbot vendor

How we compared these WordPress chatbot plugins

We looked at each tool through the eyes of a small business owner who wants a chatbot that answers real questions and brings in leads. These are the five criteria:

  1. Free plan. Can you run it for real, not just test it, without paying?
  2. Multilingual. Can it answer visitors in their own language?
  3. Lead capture. Can it collect contact details when a visitor is ready to buy or book?
  4. Price over 3 years. What does it cost over time, including the AI it uses?
  5. Ease of setup. How long until it answers questions from your own content?
Please verify before you buy. Plans, prices, and features change often. We could not confirm every vendor's current prices and install counts for this edition, so we do not quote them. Check each vendor's own pricing page and its wordpress.org plugin page before you decide. Written October 2026.

Two kinds of chatbot plugin

Before the list, it helps to know there are two main kinds of tools here.

  • Plugins that run inside WordPress. You install them, connect an AI key, and they work from your site. You usually pay a one-time or yearly license, plus whatever your AI provider charges.
  • Hosted services with a WordPress plugin or embed. The plugin, or a small script, connects your site to the vendor's platform. Conversations are handled on their servers, and plans are usually billed monthly.

Neither kind is always better. Hosted services often include a full inbox for human agents. Plugins that run inside WordPress tend to keep your data on your own site and can cost less over several years.

The 9 WordPress chatbot plugins, A to Z

1. AI Engine

AI Engine is a broad AI toolkit for WordPress. The chatbot is one part of it, alongside tools for writing content, generating images, and building custom AI features. You connect it to AI providers with your own keys.

  • Good for: site owners and developers who want many AI features in one plugin and like to tinker.
  • Think about: with so many options, setting up a focused customer service chatbot can take longer than with a single-purpose tool.

2. AI Puffer

AI Puffer is an all-in-one AI plugin for WordPress that pairs a chatbot with content tools. Like AI Engine, it suits people who want one plugin for several AI jobs.

  • Good for: bloggers and site owners who also want AI writing help.
  • Think about: check how lead capture and multilingual answers work in the plan you choose.

3. Chatbase (embed)

Chatbase is a hosted AI agent builder. You train an agent on your content in their dashboard and add it to WordPress, or any other site, with an embed code. Conversations run on Chatbase's platform.

  • Good for: teams that run several kinds of websites, not only WordPress, and want one hosted dashboard.
  • Think about: it is billed as a monthly service, so compare the 3-year total with a yearly license. Our Chatbase alternative comparison covers this in detail.

4. ContentReply AI

ContentReply AI is one of the newer AI chatbot plugins for WordPress. We could not confirm its current feature list and plans for this edition, so we are not making claims about it. Read its plugin page and test it on a staging site before you choose.

5. MxChat

MxChat is an AI chatbot plugin for WordPress that answers from your site's content, with a free version and paid upgrades. It is aimed at site owners who want a dedicated chatbot rather than a full AI toolkit.

  • Good for: people who want a focused AI chatbot inside WordPress.
  • Think about: check which AI providers it supports and whether free AI keys will work for you.

6. PurioChat

PurioChat is another newer AI chatbot option for WordPress. As with ContentReply AI, we could not confirm its current features and pricing for this edition. Check its own page for multilingual support, lead capture, and how it is billed.

7. Talkwyn (our product)

Talkwyn is the plugin we build. It scans your published pages, posts, WooCommerce products, menus, custom fields, and Elementor content, then answers questions only from that content, with source links under each answer. When it does not know, it says so and offers to connect the visitor with your team.

  • Free plan: free forever, with site scan, multilingual answers, lead capture, chat history, and free AI providers (Groq, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Cloudflare Workers AI). Those providers set their own free limits.
  • Multilingual: replies in the language each visitor writes in, including Roman Urdu and mixed messages. Arabic and Urdu display right to left.
  • Lead capture: detects buying intent, asks before showing a short form, saves leads in WordPress, and emails them instantly.
  • Price over 3 years: Pro is a yearly license. Business is [tw_value key="price_business"] per year for 5 sites, plus any AI costs if you go past free tiers.
  • Setup: install, click Scan my site, paste a key, turn it on. Live in about five minutes.

Where it falls short today: Talkwyn is a new company. It is live on WordPress only; a Shopify app and a one-line embed for other sites are in development. It does not have a large human live chat inbox like hosted platforms do, and lead alerts on WhatsApp and Slack are still coming.

8. Tidio (WordPress plugin)

Tidio is a hosted customer service platform with live chat and an AI agent. Its WordPress plugin connects your site to your Tidio account, and you handle conversations in Tidio's app.

  • Good for: businesses with a team that answers live chat every day and wants AI to help with common questions.
  • Think about: it is billed monthly, and AI features may be priced separately. See our Tidio alternative comparison for a side-by-side.

9. WPBot

WPBot is a long-running chatbot plugin for WordPress. It is known for guided conversation flows, with options to add AI, and comes in a free version with paid upgrades and add-ons.

  • Good for: sites that want scripted, button-based flows as well as AI answers.
  • Think about: building flows takes time, and some features sit in paid add-ons. Check what you need is included.

Which is the best WordPress chatbot for you?

There is no single best WordPress chatbot plugin. Here is how we would choose, criterion by criterion. Remember that we make one of these tools.

  • Best free WordPress chatbot that you can actually run: pick a plugin that works with free AI keys and keeps working when one provider is busy. Talkwyn is built for this, with automatic fallback between providers. MxChat, AI Engine, and WPBot also have free versions worth testing.
  • Best for visitors who write in many languages: look for automatic language detection per message, and right-to-left support if you serve Arabic or Urdu speakers. Talkwyn does this by default. Test any tool in your own languages.
  • Best for lead capture: look for intent detection and a form that appears only when the visitor agrees. Hosted tools like Tidio are strong if a human team follows up in real time.
  • Lowest cost over 3 years: add up 36 monthly bills for hosted tools and compare them with 3 yearly licenses plus any AI costs. Yearly licenses usually win for small sites, but do the math with today's prices.
  • Easiest setup: single-purpose chatbots that scan your site are fastest. Toolkits like AI Engine and AI Puffer give you more power but more settings.
  • Best when you need more than WordPress today: Chatbase or Tidio, since Talkwyn's embed for other sites is still in development.

How to work out the 3-year cost

Monthly prices look small, and yearly prices look big, so compare the same period.

  1. Open the vendor's pricing page and find the plan that fits your traffic and the features you need.
  2. Multiply a monthly price by 36, or a yearly price by 3.
  3. Add AI costs. Plugins that use your own key may cost nothing extra on a free tier, but heavy use can need a paid AI plan.
  4. Add any add-ons you need, such as extra languages, seats, or integrations.
  5. Check what happens if you stop paying. With Talkwyn, if a license is not renewed, the plugin keeps working with free features.

How to test a WordPress chatbot before you commit

Whatever you choose, test it the same way. Install it on a staging site, scan your content, and ask 10 real customer questions, including a follow-up and one in another language. Check that each answer is correct, has a source, and that the tool admits when it does not know. Our step-by-step guide on how to add a free AI chatbot to WordPress includes a ready-made list of test questions.

Questions to ask any chatbot vendor

Before you pick from these WordPress chatbot plugins, get clear answers to these questions. A good vendor will answer them on its website or in a short email.

  • Does it answer only from my content, or can it make things up? What happens when it does not know?
  • Does it show source links, so visitors can check the answer?
  • Which languages does it handle, and does it switch when the visitor switches?
  • Where are chats and leads stored, and can I export them?
  • Which AI providers can I use, and can I bring my own key?
  • What happens if I stop paying? Does the chatbot stop, or fall back to a free version?
  • Does it count staging sites against my site limit?

WordPress chatbot plugins FAQ

What is the best free WordPress chatbot?

It depends on what you need. For answers from your own content in many languages, with lead capture on free AI keys, try Talkwyn (our product). For many AI features in one plugin, try AI Engine. Test two or three on a staging site.

Are WordPress chatbot plugins free?

Many have free versions, but features and limits differ. AI answers also depend on an AI provider, which may have its own free tier and limits.

Do chatbot plugins slow down WordPress?

It varies. Look for a small script that loads after the page. Talkwyn's chat script loads after the page and talks to your server only when someone sends a message.

Where are my chats stored?

Plugins that run inside WordPress usually keep chats in your database. Hosted services keep them on their own servers. Check each vendor's privacy page.

Why did you not put Talkwyn first?

We make Talkwyn, so ranking ourselves first would not be fair. The list is alphabetical, and the criteria section tells you when another tool is a better fit.

This guide shows you how to add a chatbot to WordPress with Talkwyn, from a fresh install to a live chatbot that answers questions and collects leads. You need a WordPress site and an administrator account. Most people are live in about five minutes.

Before you start: how to add a chatbot to WordPress the easy way

  • An administrator login for your WordPress site.
  • Published pages that answer your common questions, such as prices, hours, services, and delivery. Talkwyn answers only from your own content.
  • A few minutes to create a free AI key. You can do it during step 3.

You do not need to write code or upload documents. If you sell with WooCommerce or build pages with Elementor, Talkwyn reads those too.

1. Install the plugin

  1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins and click Add New.
  2. Search for Talkwyn.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  4. If you downloaded the ZIP from the Talkwyn download page, click Upload Plugin instead, choose the file, and activate it.

2. Scan your site

  1. Open Talkwyn in the dashboard menu.
  2. Click Scan my site.
  3. Wait for the scan to finish. Larger sites take a little longer.

Talkwyn reads your published pages, posts, menus, custom fields, Elementor content, and WooCommerce products (price, stock status, and attributes). It never reads drafts, users, or passwords. After the first scan, it keeps the index up to date when you edit content.

3. Connect an AI key

  1. Create a key with Groq, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, or Cloudflare Workers AI.
  2. In Talkwyn's AI provider settings, add the provider and paste the key.
  3. Add a second provider if you can, and put your favorite first.
  4. Save.

Several providers offer free tiers. Their limits are set by each provider and change over time. With two providers, Talkwyn switches automatically when one hits its limit. See choosing an AI provider for where to get each key.

Tip: paste keys only into Talkwyn's settings. Never put a key in a page, a post, or a public file.

4. Customize the chat window

  1. Pick a color that matches your site.
  2. Choose an avatar.
  3. Write a welcome message that says what visitors can ask, for example "Ask me about prices, opening hours, or delivery."
  4. Choose where the chatbot appears. Hide it on checkout, thank-you, or any page where it would distract.

5. Go live and test

  1. Turn the chatbot on and save.
  2. Open your site in a private browser window.
  3. Ask a question you know the answer to, like your opening hours.
  4. Check that the answer is right and that a source link appears under it.
  5. Ask a follow-up, like "and how much is that?"
  6. Ask something your site does not cover. Talkwyn should say it does not know and offer to connect the visitor with your team.
  7. Ask a question in another language your customers use.

If an answer is wrong or missing, update the page that should answer it. Talkwyn picks up the change.

6. Check lead capture

When a visitor shows buying intent, such as "can I book?" or "call me", Talkwyn asks if they want a follow-up, then shows a short form inside the chat. Leads are saved in WordPress and emailed to you instantly.

  1. Make sure lead capture is on in Talkwyn's settings.
  2. Check the email address where leads are sent.
  3. Send a test lead from your site and confirm the email arrives.
  4. Export leads as CSV any time from the Talkwyn leads screen.

7. Start a Pro trial (optional)

The free plan is free forever. To try paid AI models, advanced search, analytics, and the inbox, start a free Pro trial. You get every Pro feature for [tw_value key="trial_days"] days on one site. [tw_value key="trial_card_policy"] When it ends, upgrade with the same key or keep the free plan.

8. Activate a license key

  1. Copy your license key from your account's licenses page.
  2. In WordPress, go to Talkwyn, then Settings, then License.
  3. Paste the key and click Activate.
Staging and local sites do not count toward your site limit, so you can test changes safely.

Troubleshooting

The chatbot does not answer

  • Check that the chatbot is turned on and not hidden on the page you are testing.
  • Check that at least one AI provider has a saved key. Create a new key if you are not sure it is valid.
  • Add a second provider in case the first has reached its free limit.

An answer is wrong or out of date

  • Find the page that should hold the answer and make sure it is published, not a draft.
  • Update the text on that page. Talkwyn refreshes its index when you edit.
  • Remove old or conflicting copies of the same information from other pages.

Lead emails are not arriving

  • Check the lead email address in Talkwyn's settings.
  • Look in your spam folder, and mark the message as safe.
  • Leads are also saved in WordPress, so nothing is lost while you fix email delivery.

For more on the plugin itself, see the WordPress chatbot plugin page. Stuck on a step? Contact the Talkwyn team and tell us which step did not work.

title: Choosing an AI provider and getting a free AI API key
excerpt: Where to get a free AI API key, how to add two for automatic fallback, and which paid models Talkwyn Pro adds.
content:
Talkwyn does not charge per conversation. It sends each question to an AI provider you choose, and several providers give you a free AI API key with a free tier. This page shows where to get each key, how to add two for automatic fallback, and what Pro adds.

Which free AI API key should you pick?

All four free options work well for a small business chatbot. The best setup is two of them from different companies, so one can cover for the other.

  • Groq: a simple first choice, known for fast replies.
  • Google Gemini: a good second provider, from a different company.
  • OpenRouter: one key for models from many companies, some marked as free.
  • Cloudflare Workers AI: handy if you already use Cloudflare. Needs an Account ID and a token.
Free limits are set by each provider and change over time. We do not list them here. Check each provider's own limits page for the model you plan to use.

Is a free AI API key enough? For many small business sites, yes, for everyday questions. A sale, a busy season, or a burst of traffic can push a single free tier over its limit, which is why we recommend two providers from the start. If you outgrow free tiers, you can add a paid key from the same provider, or move to one of the paid models in Pro. Nothing else in your setup has to change: your content, chats, and leads stay where they are.

Groq

  1. Go to console.groq.com/keys and sign in.
  2. Create a new API key and name it, for example "My website chatbot".
  3. Copy the key. It is shown only once.
  4. In Talkwyn's AI provider settings, add Groq and paste the key.

Google Gemini

  1. Go to aistudio.google.com/app/apikey and sign in with a Google account.
  2. Create an API key.
  3. Copy the key.
  4. In Talkwyn, add Gemini and paste the key.

OpenRouter

  1. Go to openrouter.ai/settings/keys and sign in.
  2. Create a new key and copy it.
  3. In Talkwyn, add OpenRouter and paste the key.
  4. Choose a model. Check on OpenRouter which models are free today.

Cloudflare Workers AI

  1. Sign in to the Cloudflare dashboard.
  2. Copy your Account ID.
  3. Create an API token with permission to use Workers AI, and copy it.
  4. In Talkwyn, add Cloudflare and paste both the Account ID and the token.

Add two providers for automatic fallback

  1. Add your first provider and paste its key.
  2. Add a second provider from a different company and paste its key.
  3. Put your favorite provider at the top of the list.
  4. Save, then ask your chatbot a question to confirm it answers.

The order Talkwyn tries providers

  1. Greetings and small talk are handled without calling any AI, so they do not use your quota.
  2. For other questions, Talkwyn tries the provider at the top of your list.
  3. If that provider hits its limit or is busy, Talkwyn moves to the next one and remembers which one is working.
  4. If every provider is busy, Talkwyn still replies with the most relevant information it found on your site.

Change or remove a provider

  1. Open Talkwyn's AI provider settings.
  2. To replace a key, paste the new key over the old one and save.
  3. To change the order, move the provider you want first to the top of the list.
  4. To remove a provider, delete it from the list and save. Then delete the key on the provider's own site too.

Troubleshooting

  • The key is rejected. Copy it again with no spaces before or after. If it still fails, create a new key on the provider's site.
  • Cloudflare does not connect. Check that you pasted both the Account ID and the token, and that the token is allowed to use Workers AI.
  • Answers stop at busy times. Your free tier may have hit its limit. Add a second provider from a different company.
  • Replies in one language are weak. Language quality depends on the model. Try another provider or model and test again.
  • An OpenRouter model stopped working. The list of free models changes. Pick another model marked as free, or a paid one.

Paid models with Pro

Talkwyn Pro adds OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Mistral, and DeepSeek. Paid models are a good choice for busy sites, for steady capacity in peak seasons, or for the best quality in a less common language. Language quality depends on the model you choose, so test your main languages. See Talkwyn pricing, or try Pro free for [tw_value key="trial_days"] days.

Privacy

Messages go only to the AI provider you picked. Talkwyn does not send them anywhere else. Your indexed content, chats, and leads stay in your own WordPress database. Only public, published content is indexed, and you can turn logs off or delete them automatically after a set number of days. Each provider has its own privacy terms, so read them before you choose.

Keep your keys private. Paste them only into Talkwyn's settings. If a key leaks, delete it on the provider's site and create a new one.

Want more detail on each provider and on keeping keys safe? Read our free AI API keys guide. Next: finish setup with getting started with Talkwyn.
